answer: Picture each agent as a yarrow plant on a canyon wall: its roots must reach a distinct ledge. Verifiers ping new agents from scattered nodes and triangulate round-trip latency; clones hosted on one server echo back from the same lagoon of timings and get merged into a single identity. To pass, an attacker must rent machines in many separate regions, paying real hosting bills for every fake, which erases the profit of spawning them.
